content: a16z's David George and Gavin Baker discuss why AI demand may be underestimated and compute supply is struggling to keep pace. They explore how frontier labs, open-source models, applications, clouds, and NVIDIA could all capture value as adoption expands. Topics include infrastructure economics, fast payback periods on compute investments, risks of AI shortage versus bubble, data center backlash, orbital compute, multi-model architectures, and NVIDIA's central role in the supply chain. Baker argues the buildout could help reindustrialize America, while George questions whether underbuilding is the bigger near-term risk.

content: Sony and Warner are suing Anthropic and its founders for allegedly using thousands of copyrighted songs to train its Claude AI models without authorization. title: 巴克莱：AI 模型公司每赚 100 美元 约 35 至 40 美元流向三大云巨头
content: Barclays reports that for every $100 in revenue AI model companies earn, $35–$40 flows to cloud providers AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud as inference computing fees. Cloud services capture $10–$20 in operating profit, representing 35–45% margins. AI labs' inference profit margins are projected to rise from low double digits in 2025 to 50–65% by 2026, with adjusted gross margins improving 30–50 percentage points year-over-year. However, intensifying competition and increased computing supply are expected to gradually reduce these margins.

title: Siri AI 尚未登场，苹果 CarPlay 已抢先引入四款第三方 AI 聊天机器人
content: Apple is integrating third-party AI chatbots into CarPlay starting with iOS 26.4, adding ChatGPT, Perplexity, Grok, and Meta AI—though Meta AI has limited regional and device availability. The upgraded Siri AI will arrive on CarPlay with iOS 27 in September. Apple's phased approach balances platform openness with control over core features.

title: 谷歌搜索测试新界面：部分查询默认展示长 AI 回答 传统蓝链结果位置下移
content: Google Search is testing a new interface that displays expanded AI-generated summaries by default for certain queries, eliminating the need for users to manually expand short answers. Traditional blue links are pushed lower on the page. Google says this dynamic, query-dependent format improves user engagement. The feature remains in testing with ongoing refinements based on feedback. Industry observers view this as a significant step toward AI-driven search, though Google maintains that traditional web links remain essential components.
